senses.def: capable of being put to use
ex: usable byproducts

senses.def: fit or ready for use or service
ex: the lawnmower is a bit rusty but still usable
2000 square feet of usable office space

senses.def: the customary manner in which a language (or a form of a language) is spoken or written
ex: English usage
a usage borrowed from French

senses.def: put into service; make work or employ for a particular purpose or for its inherent or natural purpose
ex: use your head!
we only use Spanish at home
I can't use this tool
She uses drugs rarely

senses.def: seek or achieve an end by using to one's advantage
ex: She uses her influential friends to get jobs
The president's wife used her good connections
use care when going down the stairs
use your common sense

senses.def: habitually do something or be in a certain state or place (use only in the past tense)
ex: She used to call her mother every week but now she calls only occasionally
I used to get sick when I ate in that dining hall
They used to vacation in the Bahamas
ballet is beautiful but what use is it?
he put his knowledge to good use
patrons have their uses
the principle of surprise is the most used and misused of all the principles of war
after going out of his way to help his friend get the job he felt not appreciated but used

senses.def: previously used or owned by another
ex: bought a secondhand (or used) car
the girl felt motherly and useful
a useful job
a useful member of society
extra money could be usefully spent on this project

senses.def: the quality of being of practical use
having no beneficial use or incapable of functioning usefully
ex: a kitchen full of useless gadgets
she is useless in an emergency
the furniture was sitting around uselessly

senses.def: the quality of having no practical use
a person who makes use of a thing; someone who uses or employs something
a person who uses something or someone selfishly or unethically
take (someone) to their seats, as in theaters or auditoriums
ex: he ushered us to our seats

senses.def: an official stationed at the entrance of a courtroom or legislative chamber
an act that exploits or victimizes someone (treats them unfairly)
occurring or encountered or experienced or observed frequently or in accordance with regular practice or procedure
ex: grew the usual vegetables
the usual summer heat
came at the usual time
the usual greeting
usually she was late

senses.def: seize and take control without authority and possibly with force; take as one's right or possession
ex: he usurped my rights
gloom had usurped mirth at the party after the news of the terrorist act broke
